faqs.a:
(a)
Any animal exhibiting behavior set forth in this section is hereby declared to be
               a nuisance animal. It shall be unlawful for any owner or custodian of an animal to
               allow said animal to:
(1)
Create a disturbance by loud and persistent or habitual barking, howling, yelping,
               or other unreasonable noise; or
(2)
Cause offensive or noxious odors or exhibit any other conduct or create any other
               condition which disturbs the peace, safety, or comfort of a neighborhood.
(b)
It shall not be a defense to a violation of this section that the animal owner or
               custodian was not available to remedy such violation.
(c)
For purposes of this section, persons cannot provoke the howling, barking, or other
               unreasonable noise of an animal by the ordinary or reasonable use of private properties,
               public roadways, sidewalks, or alleyways, or common areas of condominiums, townhouses,
               apartment buildings.
(d)
No summons and complaint shall be issued nor shall there be a conviction for violation
               of
section 14-53
(a)(1) unless there are at least two or more complaining witnesses from separate households
               who shall have signed such complaint and shall testify at trial.
Exception:
(1)
An animal management officer who has personally investigated the complaint of a single
               complainant and observed the nature and duration of the noise created by the animal
               may testify to his observations. Said testimony shall satisfy the requirement for
               the second complaining witness.
(2)
Where a complainant presents to the animal management officer at the time of the complaint
               other credible corroborative evidence of the alleged violation (such as a videotape),
               said evidence, if admissible, shall satisfy the requirement for the second complaining
               witness.
(Code 1981, § 6-32; Ord. No. 3496, § 2, 12-14-1998)
